page: Amazon Web Services c5n.large is a compute-optimized instance utilizing the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8124M processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, supported by 5.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the c5n.large sits primarily in the lower tiers for compute and memory throughput. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated as weak at 1396.99, while the multi-core performance falls into the poor category at 1834.59. Memory bandwidth tests show poor results, with read-only large block speeds at 13.56 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.83 GB/sec. However, single-threaded gzip compression achieves an average rating of 23.89 GB/sec. Redis SET operations reach 1.83 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 2.13 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c5n.large offers a dedicated Intel Xeon compute profile with enhanced network capabilities at a lower entry point, though its resource density is constrained by the 5.0 GB memory limit. Given the benchmark profile, this instance is best suited for lightweight compute tasks, basic network-bound operations, single-threaded compression utilities, and entry-level web serving where high memory capacity is not required.
